messages:
aj: Heads up — us-west GPU pool is at ~98% slot saturation right now, streaming connections are holding the queue and sync jobs are timing out. Anyone seen this exact behavior before?

maria: saw the spike at ~08:12 UTC, short window but stream RPS jumped after the websocket keepalive tweak. Queue depth for sync requests went from ~20 -> ~250.

david: is this the friday incident replay or a new pattern? autoscaler logs looked normal when I checked.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_up initiated for pool=us-west-gpu, delta=+8 nodes, request_id=scale-1769003478 (provisioning)

linh: Looks related to long-lived streamed connections that hold concurrency budget for the lifetime of the socket. Proposal: change admission-control to be duration-aware — give streams a higher per-socket cost (eg multiplier) and let short sync requests have lower cost.

sre-oncall: short-term mitigation idea: flip streaming admission to "soft-limit" so we stop rejecting short syncs; that will allow preemption when the overall queue depth crosses thresholds. I can toggle for us-west for 30m.

maria: preemption worries me — active streaming sessions will see dropped frames. For customer-facing realtime apps that is bad. Could we instead implement graceful degrade: convert affected streams to chunked polling mode (non-streaming) before killing?

david: another angle — add a priority tier: realtime (short sync), interactive streaming, background. Admission-control picks by priority and current budget. That lets us avoid wholesale preemption. Also cheaper than adding nodes.

aj: logs show enforcement decisions: ```
2026-03-18T08:15:22Z rt-runtime admit=false reason=concurrency_budget stream_conn=true conn_id=abc123 pool=us-west-gpu
2026-03-18T08:15:22Z rt-runtime admit=true reason=priority_override stream_conn=false req_id=sync-zz789
```

autoscaler: autoscaler: scale_up halted — region quota near limit (GPUs 28/30). Please open infra-aws if we need immediate quota raise.

linh: For an engineering fix, I'm going to prototype a token-lease approach: streams take a shorter-lived lease (expire after idle-ms) and renew on activity. If we detect long idle streaming sockets we reclaim their token. Also per-tenant stream caps so noisy tenants don't starve pool.

sre-oncall: I'll flip the soft-limit now for us-west and set an alert: if sync-error-rate > 1% or p50 latency > 250ms rollback. @maria can you watch the dashboard?

maria: On it — created a watch and a pager rule to this channel. Also added a temporary dashboard tile: stream_concurrency_by_tenant and stream_idle_seconds. :mag_right:

aj: Can ops add a runbook blurb? Quick steps: 1) set runtime.streaming.multiplier=4 2) enable runtime.streaming.soft_limit=true 3) fallback route: non-streaming chunked for eligible clients.

david: cost tradeoff: adding +8 nodes would fix latency but costs ~+$6k/month per extra node. If we can solve with priority routing + token leases it's much cheaper.

linh: I'll start a canary change: reduce per-stream multiplier from 10 -> 5 in canary us-west/az-b for 10% traffic and measure. Will post results.

sre-oncall: update: soft-limit enabled at 08:22 UTC. Monitoring.

maria: initial look: sync p95 improved, stream p50 increased slightly but still within SLA for most tenants. Detailed numbers in dashboard.

aj: Thanks everyone. Let's follow-up with a short RFC for admission-control changes and a small runbook entry for stream saturation incidents.

maria: filing RFC now and adding runbook to eng-runbooks. Will ping when done. :white_check_mark:
